text: Spawn in vestibule (--rooms all): an empty black bar at top-center (x370-910,y45-96) covers the end of the objective line ('...Screen ro|om's left-hand door'). Objective also reads 'NEXT Next: ...' (doubled) and still tells me to go through the Screen room door although I already stand in the small room. tick 1565

List room: the 'Find a row that isn't there' plaque stands behind the desk; the desk blocks approach so its body text stays tiny/blurry even at closest reach (could only half-read it from ~6m at full zoom). Key instructions (set switches, press CHECK) only legible via the caption.

First CHECK (row 10000000): board outlines in red the tile where my row differs from each of rows 1-8, prints 'differs at tile N' per row, then reveals 'row 7033 ... starts just like yours' and 'You'd have to check forever.' Clear, satisfying feedback. Note the red outlines are scattered (first difference), not on the diagonal, so they don't point a newcomer at the trick.

After the first win the librarian inserts my row as row 1 and shifts the rest down; NOW the board outlines the diagonal (row n, tile n) in gold. This is the key hint, but it only appears in round 2, after the player has already beaten round 1 (by luck or by knowing the trick). In round 1 nothing pointed at the diagonal.

Debrief 'No list holds them all.' explains the diagonal construction plainly and links it to Cantor 1891 (bigger infinities), Godel ('I am not on the list of things arithmetic can prove') and Turing halting. Clear for a newcomer. Minor: 'What just happened' asserts 'You built your row from the list itself' even if a player won by trial and error.
